en: Andres Bonifacio founded the secret revolutionary society called the Katipunan to gain Philippine independence from Spain.
The Philippine Supreme Court, the highest court in the land, consists of one Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest eagles in the world.
General Emilio Aguinaldo officially proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish colonial rule on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo, Aklan, honors the Santo Niño through vibrant street dancing and indigenous-inspired costumes.
The Ifugao indigenous group carved the magnificent Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of the Cordilleras over two thousand years ago.
Baybayin is the ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system where characters represent syllables rather than individual consonants and vowels.
Dr. Fe del Mundo, the first female professor at Harvard Medical School, invented a bamboo incubator for rural areas.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, all citizens who are at least eighteen years old have the right to vote.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the famous Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan and the iconic UP Oblation statue.
The Filipino value of bayanihan originated from the tradition of neighbors helping a family move their entire nipa hut.
